about: Checks before merging the MI210 rows into the Φ-Bench dataset that no script can decide. status: done | open | failed | not-applicable. blocking: the row is not ready while the item is not done. task null applies to every row. Read by phibench_premerge.py.

items.note: Clear the rows, their reference patches and the vendored code with Omar and the other Φ-Bench owners before merging. The Hugging Face copy is already public (the user's choice, 2026-11-07). Deferred by the user (2026-11-09): to settle later, before a merge.

The draft dataset says apache-2.0, unconfirmed. Vendored code under environment/repo/ is from vLLM (Apache-2.0); the task text, grader and patches are ours. Deferred by the user (2026-11-09): to settle later, before a merge.

Upstream builds with docker buildx. Our nodes have no Docker access (the docker socket needs a group we are not in) and only Apptainer, which cannot build from a Dockerfile. The images were built with Enroot by following each Dockerfile step (phibench_enroot.py) and every Dockerfile check passed. A docker buildx build has to be done by whoever merges, on a machine with Docker (user, 2026-11-09).

scripts/run_task.py now has an amd GPU mode (/dev/kfd, /dev/dri, seccomp unconfined, group video; GPU subset through HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES), chosen automatically when task.toml gpu_types are AMD. NVIDIA hosts and NVIDIA tasks behave as before (unit tests). Shipped as scripts/run_task.py with scripts/run_task-amd.patch for upstream, which applies with git apply to their revision 3bcefac. Checked with --dry-run only: Docker is not available on our nodes. The owners still have to accept the change.

Our Dockerfile copies tests/verifier-correctness-manifest.json, with ref_speedup, into the image, as upstream's own example lh task does; upstream's README says the in-image copy omits the anchor. Ask the owners which they want.
Upstream anchors are calibrated on NVIDIA H20; ours on AMD MI210. With no hardware column, MI210 is stated in the summary, instruction, task.toml and caveat. The owners decide whether that is enough.
